Raising the target range to 4.75–5% and continuing QT is a restrictive stance broadly consistent with Taylor-rule behavior often documented for central banks. The statement’s emphasis that “recent developments are likely to result in tighter credit conditions” aligns with the Bernanke-Gertler broad credit channel and the Kashyap-Stein bank-lending channel: banking stress tightens lending standards and amplifies the contractionary impact of rate hikes on spending, hiring, and inflation. The Committee’s focus on cumulative tightening and policy lags reflects the real-time uncertainty highlighted by Orphanides, while the reliance on administered rates and standing facilities (including IORB and ON RRP) follows operating-procedures frameworks discussed by Goodfriend. Ongoing balance-sheet runoff of Treasuries and MBS can work through term premia and the yield curve (as in Cochrane and Piazzesi), further tightening financial conditions. Net effect: hawkish on inflation but tempered by recognition of financial headwinds—slightly more negative for near-term growth than a pure rate-hike signal alone.
